items.title: Four takeaways from Nvidia's first earnings report after Jensen Huang scandal
items.take: Nvidia's first report since Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation beat again, but the SEC opened an inquiry into whether its disclosures gave investors a complete picture, and leadership ruled out his return. U.S. stocks fell as AI doubts festered, with the S&P 500 down 1.6% and Nvidia off roughly 24% this month.

items.title: Anthropic Approaches Final IPO Hurdle After Tech Stocks Decline
items.take: Anthropic prices potentially the biggest IPO ever tonight after guiding investors above its $70-to-$78 range, aiming for a valuation near $1.4 trillion. Shares trade Thursday on Nasdaq under ANT, with Google and Nvidia each putting $10 billion in alongside the deal.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Shake Hands as Leaders Gather in China: Live Updates
items.take: Trump landed in Shenzhen to a rare airport hug from Xi, and the three nuclear-armed leaders' first-ever trilateral summit comes Thursday on APEC's sidelines. Nuclear arms control is the marquee topic, though analysts see little chance of a breakthrough.

items.title: U.S. officially loses measles elimination status amid ongoing outbreaks
items.take: The Pan American Health Organization revoked the U.S. measles-elimination status earned in 2000, after 12 straight months of transmission and more than 5,400 cases this year, the worst outbreak since 1991. It leads every front page this morning, from the Times to USA Today to the Globe.

items.title: Nvidia Moves On From Jensen Huang
items.take: Today's WSJ podcast leads with Nvidia's post-Huang earnings call: the beat was clean, but the SEC inquiry and the question of who replaces him hung over the tape. Also on the show, Trump's return to the world stage in Asia.
